title: Ecruteak City
subtitle: & the Burned Tower
epigraph: A Historical City — Where the Past Meets the Present
summary: Find Morty at the Burned Tower, pick up Surf at the Dance Theater and win the Fog Badge.
where: Route 37 ends at a wooden gate, and beyond it the streets turn to old stone. Ecruteak is Johto's city of two towers: one burned long ago and still standing in ruins on the north-west terrace, the other rising behind a guarded gatehouse to the north.

Everything you need for this chapter is inside the city walls. The Gym is in the south-west corner, but you won't get in straight away — its Leader has gone to the Burned Tower, and a sage is minding the door until he's back.

objective.title: Win the Fog Badge
objective.text: The Gym door is blocked while Morty is away. Meet him inside the Burned Tower, see what's waiting in its basement, then come back and take on the Gym.

quick.d: Speak to Bill by the counter while you're there.
Beat the Rocket Grunt on stage. The gentleman in the audience hands you HM Surf.
North-west terrace. Meet Eusine and Morty just inside.
Walk toward the gap in the floor. After the battle the floor gives way.
Then climb the ladder in the north-east corner and leave the tower.
South-west corner of the city. Follow the unseen path and defeat Morty.
Route 38 leads on toward Olivine City.

steps.title: Settle in
body: Start at the Pokémon Center, the red-roofed building in the middle of the south row. On your first visit a man is standing at the counter: that's Bill, who has just finished tuning the Storage System. Talk to him and he heads home to Goldenrod.
One door west of the Center is a small house with a single resident. He has a question for you — answer Yes and he gives you the Dowsing Machine, which pings when a hidden item is close by.
Before you leave the streets, climb the steps to the Burned Tower's terrace in the north-west. A Rare Candy is sitting out in the open, left of the tower door.

callouts.title: Dowsing Machine
callouts.text: Free from the man in the house west of the Pokémon Center. It tells you an item is near, not exactly where — you still have to search the spot yourself.

callouts.title: Rare Candy
callouts.text: Item ball on the Burned Tower terrace, just left of the entrance.

steps.title: The Dance Theater
body: The large hall in the middle of the city is the Ecruteak Dance Theater, home of the Kimono Girls. The first time you step inside, a Team Rocket Grunt is on the stage heckling the dancer.
Walk up and talk to him to start the battle. He isn't much of a threat, but he does carry two Full Restores, so expect the fight to drag a little.
Once he's gone, the gentleman in the audience is so impressed that he gives you HM Surf. If he doesn't approach you on your way out, just talk to him.

callouts.title: HM Surf
callouts.text: From the gentleman in the Dance Theater after you beat the Rocket Grunt. You can't Surf outside of battle until you hold the Fog Badge.

steps.title: The Burned Tower
body: Go through the tower door and a stranger greets you at once. This is Eusine, who has spent years chasing a Pokémon called Suicune; Morty is here with him, investigating the tower. Neither of them will battle you.

Two Trainers are picking through the rubble on this floor — a Firebreather near the top and a Burglar on the west side — and there are two items worth the detour: an HP Up in the south-east and an Ether in the north-west.
When you're ready, walk toward the broken floor in the middle of the room. Your Rival is waiting beside it, and he is not in a good mood.

boss.title: Rival
strategy: His strongest Pokémon is always the starter that has the edge over yours. Keep something in reserve that resists it.
Golbat knows Confuse Ray. Switching out clears the confusion if it starts costing you turns.
He carries one Super Potion, so don't be surprised if a nearly beaten Pokémon bounces back once.

after: The moment the battle is over, the damaged floor gives way and you drop into the basement.

spoiler.label: What happens in the basement
body: Three Pokémon are resting in the chamber below — Raikou, Entei and Suicune. As you land they stir, and each one bolts in a different direction before you can do a thing. Eusine runs in a moment too late and is thrilled anyway.
You can't battle them here. Wherever they've gone, they're no longer in the tower.

after2: Before you climb out, look around the basement: an Ultra Ball lies on the west side, and TM Taunt is in the south-west corner. A pushable boulder sits near the TM — if it's in your way and you can't move it yet, come back later.
The ladder out is in the north-east corner. Back on the ground floor the hole you fell through stays open, and Morty and Eusine have gone.

callouts.title: Burned Tower items
callouts.text: 1F: HP Up, Ether. B1F: Ultra Ball, TM Taunt.

steps.title: Ecruteak Gym
body: With the tower business finished, the sage outside the Gym is gone and the door is open.

Inside, the hall is pitch black apart from a few lit platforms. A narrow walkway links them, but you can't see it. Step off the edge and you're sent back to the entrance. Move one tile at a time and trust the line the platforms suggest — as one of the Gym Trainers puts it, the path is right in front of your eyes.
Four Trainers stand on the platforms. Each one is a short fight, and every one of them uses Ghost- or Dark-type Pokémon, and Normal- and Fighting-type moves pass straight through the ghosts.

puzzle.title: The unseen path
puzzle.text: Every tile marked below is a pitfall that sends you back to the door. The safe route runs through the gaps between them.

callouts.title: Battle the Gym Trainers first
callouts.text: Any Gym Trainer you haven't fought stands down for good once Morty is beaten. If you want the experience and prize money, take them on before the Leader.

boss.title: Gym Leader Morty
boss.tagline: The Mystic Seer of the Future
strategy: Three of his four Pokémon know Hypnosis. Bring a way to cure sleep, or lead with a Pokémon that can't be put to sleep.
Stantler is the odd one out: a Normal-type among ghosts. Ghost-type moves won't touch it, but Fighting-type moves hit it hard. This is the "mystic deer" the Gym guide warns you about.
Misdreavus uses Perish Song. Count the turns and switch before the timer runs out.

Gengar is his ace and holds a Sitrus Berry. It pairs Mean Look with Hypnosis and Dream Eater, so don't leave a sleeping Pokémon in front of it — and don't bother with Ground-type moves, since it has Levitate.
Dark- and Ghost-type attacks are your best tools against the three ghosts.

after: Morty hands over the Fog Badge and TM Shadow Ball. From now on you can use Surf outside of battle.

optional.title: Ecruteak after dark
optional.text: Visit at night and the streets fill with Gastly, Haunter and Misdreavus drifting between the lanterns. They're only there for atmosphere — you can't battle them — but it's the best time to see the city.

optional.title: The Tin Tower gatehouse
optional.text: The tall building at the north end of the city is the barrier station to the Tin Tower. The sage inside turns you away for now. Remember where it is; you'll be back.

optional.title: Listen to the locals
optional.text: Two rumours are doing the rounds: the Pokémon that lights Olivine's Lighthouse has fallen ill, and something is rampaging at the Lake of Rage. Both are places you'll be visiting.

unlocks.title: Surf in the field
unlocks.text: The Fog Badge lets you use Surf outside of battle. Water routes are now open to you.

unlocks.title: Level 50 obedience
unlocks.text: Morty tells you Pokémon up to Lv. 50 will now obey you.

unlocks.title: Bill's PC
unlocks.text: After you meet Bill in the Pokémon Center, the Storage System carries his name.

unlocks.title: Three roaming legends
unlocks.text: The three Pokémon from the Burned Tower basement have left the city.

next.title: Olivine City
next.text: Take the gatehouse on the west side of the city, past the pair of stone lanterns. Routes 38 and 39 run past farmland down to the coast and Olivine City, where the Lighthouse rumour is waiting to be looked into.
next.alt: The east gate opens onto Route 42 and the road toward Mahogany Town, if you'd rather explore first.
